heading: Delhi High Court protects Kajol's personality rights, orders obscene content removal
paragraphs: The Delhi High Court has passed an interim order protecting the personality rights of Bollywood actor Kajol.

The court restrained several entities from using her name, image, likeness, or other personality traits for commercial purposes, including the sale of merchandise. It also directed the immediate takedown of obscene and pornographic material published against the actor.
The High Court further observed that it would pass appropriate orders to prevent misuse of Kajol's identity through artificial intelligence tools, including deepfakes.

The Delhi High Court has, in a series of similar matters, granted protection to several public figures against the unauthorised commercial exploitation of their identity. Coordinate benches have previously safeguarded the personality rights of Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and actor Pawan Kalyan, former cricketer Sunil Gavaskar, and actors R Madhavan and NT Rama Rao Jr. A similar plea has also been moved by actor Salman Khan.

In other cases, the court has extended relief to spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Telugu actor Nagarjuna, Bollywood actors Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and Abhishek Bachchan, as well as filmmaker Karan Johar.

The High Court has also issued a John Doe order in favour of podcaster Raj Shamani, noting his prominence in India’s digital content space and restraining unknown parties from misusing his name, image, or likeness.
